# Authorization foundation — execution plan
_Supersedes the thin-skills plan. S0 spike DONE & validated (see M0)._

## 1. Guarantee
An agent reads within its scope, but data never reaches a user (or leaves) beyond what that user can access in the source systems (Slack channels, GitHub repos, …). Mirror the source live; sharing happens in the source, not in Lobu. Collaborative = strict intersection. Personal/Mac (local Owletto) is a separate surface, out of scope.

## 2. Architecture spine (validated)
The agent submits *intent* (SQL / search / channel request) and never holds a raw DB handle. The server injects the scoping predicate **below the tool**, so enforcement is deterministic SQL, not LLM-dependent or bypassable (CTE-wrapped, schema-qualified refs rejected, READ ONLY). One `AuthzScope{org, principal, agentId, policyVersion}` → one compiler → injected at **all four read seams** (SQL `buildScopedQuery`, recall `search-path`, content `get_content`, conversation store). Effective = **agent-scope ∩ requesting-user source-memberships ∩ provenance**, fail-closed. Principal = `$member` (reuse `entity_identities`, verified subset). Access-memberships come from per-source **adapters** (Slack/GitHub → a relation store keyed on `$member`), kept fresh via webhooks + reconcile. Egress/provenance covers only the residuals (cached derivations, aggregates) — live reads are covered by the seam filter.

## 3. Planning method
- **Thin vertical slices**, each independently shippable and **verified on the embedded-PG integration harness** (proven in M0 — auto-spawns Postgres, runs migrations).
- **Per-seam negative deny-test is a merge blocker** for any read-path change.
- **Front-load the gating decisions** (§5) before the milestone that needs them.
- Standalone bug-fixes ship first, decoupled from the feature.
- Acceptance = the red-team corpus (§6), grown per milestone.

`check-drift` fails on **every open lobu PR** whenever `owletto/main` has commits past the pinned
submodule SHA:

```
owletto/main has merged commits past the pinned SHA. The parent bump PR is missing.
Pinned:       <sha>
owletto/main: <sha>
Fix (open as a separate PR): ... git commit -m 'chore(submodule): bump owletto to current main'
```

**Do NOT blindly follow that suggested fix.** If `owletto/main`'s tip contains a UI change whose
lobu-side pointer PR is still waiting on `/ui-approve`, opening a separate bump PR to that tip would
**ship the unapproved UI to prod** — routing around the `ui-review` gate rather than satisfying it.
In that situation the pending human approval IS the drift fix. Stop and say so; don't "unblock" it.

There is no partial escape either: pinning an *earlier* ancestor (e.g. only the infra commits) leaves
the UI commit still past the pin, so check-drift keeps failing. The pointer must reach the tip.

Seen 2026-08-05: my own owletto k8s merges (#725–#731) pushed `owletto/main` ahead and broke
check-drift on 4 lobu PRs at once. Three pointer PRs were open simultaneously, each pinning a
different point in owletto history and each needing its OWN ui-review approval — merge order matters
and only the last one reaches the tip:

| lobu PR | pins | note |
|---|---|---|
| #2508 | `ef0ffc1e` | oldest |
| #2509 | `776eb120` | |
| #2511 | `400bcb14` | = owletto/main tip, the one that actually clears drift |

**Diagnostic reflex:** a PR failing only `check-drift` almost never has a problem of its own. Confirm
with `gh api /repos/lobu-ai/lobu/pulls/<n>/files --jq '.[] | select(.filename=="packages/owletto") | .patch'`
to read what each pointer PR pins (`gh pr diff | grep Subproject` does NOT work — the submodule hunk
is not in the text diff), and `git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> <tip>` to order them. Don't spend a
CI cycle "fixing" the PR itself.

Merging an Owletto PR advances `owletto/main` past the SHA that `lobu/main`
pins. `check-drift` then fails on **every open lobu PR in the repo**, not just
the one carrying the bump — it compares the pinned SHA against `owletto/main`
and cannot pass until a pointer bump lands on `lobu/main`.

Done 2026-08-05 (owletto#723 merged while its parent lobu#2509 was still
waiting on a human `/ui-approve`): six open PRs went red on a check none of
their authors could fix.

**Why:** check-drift's own rule says the pinned SHA must be reachable from
`owletto/main`, which reads like "merge owletto first". It is the opposite. The
pointer PR carries the bump, so the safe order is:

1. Get the parent lobu PR fully green **including `ui-review` approval**.
2. Merge the Owletto PR.
3. Repin to the merged SHA, push, let check-drift go green.
4. Merge the parent.

Holding the Owletto PR open scopes the red to your own PR (pinned SHA not
reachable) instead of blocking everyone.

**How to apply:** before `gh pr merge` on an owletto PR, check whether the
parent lobu PR can merge in the same sitting. If it is blocked on a human gate,
leave the submodule PR open.

  so it always reschedules even on error.

  alone does not explain both.
